title: Lists: commas vs. semicolons for series items
subtitle: Boundaries · 15 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **15 of the official questions in Boundaries are this one** — 4 Easy, 1 Medium, 10 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The sentence names a group of things ('these include...', 'known for...', 'works include...').
- The blank falls between two list items.
- The choices offer a comma, a semicolon, a colon, or a period.
- Look past the blank for a later semicolon, or for items that already contain commas or 'which' clauses.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Scan the rest of the sentence for how the other items are separated.
- 2) If any item has internal commas, or the other separators are semicolons, use a semicolon.
- 3) If the items are simple and separated by commas, use a comma.
- Match the separator the sentence already uses.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The internal comma inside a long item makes a comma look natural at the blank.
This subtype is designed to punish you for deciding from the local words alone instead of checking how the rest of the list is punctuated.
